headline: SK Hynix will spend about 38 billion dollars on two new memory chip plants in South Korea to meet AI demand.
score_reason: Large, official capacity commitment by a key AI memory supplier, but announced on Friday 2 Oct, before today's window, and relayed second hand.
importance_line: More DRAM and NAND capacity from 2027 onward matters to everyone waiting on AI hardware and to Nvidia and other buyers of high-speed memory, though the first plant only breaks ground next July and the market sold the shares down on the day.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by Stocktwits, that SK Hynix announced on Friday 2 Oct 2026 a 54 trillion won (about $38 billion) plan for a new DRAM fab at Yongin and a NAND flash plant at Cheongju, with roughly two-thirds of the money going to DRAM, the fast memory that AI processors depend on. The Yongin plant is the second of four planned there, with groundbreaking set for July 2027, and the announcement follows a wider $880 billion pledge by SK, Samsung and the Korean government to double the country's memory output within five years.
notes: Stocktwits is a copy site relaying Bloomberg; original Bloomberg link not available, url is where the text was read. Score lowered from 6 to 5 because the event predates 3 Oct.
